frontMatter.welcome:
Dear Employee,
It gives us immense pleasure to welcome you to JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd.
As part of our organization, you are joining a team that is built on a strong foundation of quality, innovation, integrity, and sustainability. Our companies are committed to delivering excellence in the fields of pharmaceutical excipients and specialty wax products, serving customers across diverse industries while maintaining the highest standards of safety and responsibility.
At JRS Pharma and Gujarat Microwax, we firmly believe that our employees are our most valuable asset. The growth and success of our organization are directly linked to the dedication, skills, and passion of our people. We are committed to providing a work environment that is safe, inclusive, and supportive, where every individual is encouraged to grow both professionally and personally.
This Employee Handbook has been designed to help you understand our policies, values, and expectations, as well as the resources available to support your journey with us. It outlines our commitment to employee well-being, ethical practices, and continuous improvement.
We encourage you to actively participate, share your ideas, and uphold the values that define our organization. Together, we aim to achieve sustainable growth while making a positive impact on our employees, customers, and the community.
We look forward to your valuable contribution and wish you a successful and fulfilling career with us.
Warm regards, Management JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd.
frontMatter.about:
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. together represent a strong combination of global expertise and local manufacturing excellence, delivering high-quality products to pharmaceutical, food, and industrial sectors.
JRS Pharma, a division of the globally recognized JRS Group, specializes in the development and manufacturing of high-quality pharmaceutical excipients. With a strong focus on innovation, functionality, and regulatory compliance, JRS Pharma supports pharmaceutical manufacturers worldwide by providing advanced excipient solutions that enhance drug performance, stability, and patient safety. The company operates with a commitment to international quality standards, continuous research, and sustainable practices.
Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd., on the other hand, is a well-established manufacturer of specialty waxes and petroleum-based products in India. The company offers a diverse range of products including microcrystalline wax, paraffin wax, and customized wax blends that cater to industries such as pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, packaging, rubber, and candles. With a strong emphasis on quality control, process efficiency, and customer satisfaction, Gujarat Microwax has built a reputation for reliability and consistency in both domestic and international markets.
Together, the organizations operate with a shared commitment to:
- Quality Excellence – Ensuring all products meet stringent national and international standards
- Innovation & Technology – Continuously improving processes and product performance
- Sustainability – Promoting environmentally responsible manufacturing practices
- Customer Focus – Delivering value-driven solutions tailored to client needs
- Employee Well-being – Creating a safe, inclusive, and growth-oriented workplace
By combining global

JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. is committed to maintaining a professional, ethical, safe, transparent, and employee-focused workplace environment that supports operational excellence, innovation, sustainability, and long-term organizational growth. These policies apply to all individuals working for or representing JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd., including:
- Permanent employees
- Probationary employees
- Temporary employees
- Contract employees
- Trainees and apprentices
- Interns
- Consultants
- Third-party personnel working within company premises
Every employee is expected to read, understand, acknowledge, and comply with the policies and procedures contained in this handbook throughout the duration of employment.

chapters.title: Equal Employment Opportunity Policy
chapters.text:
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. is firmly committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without discrimination, favoritism, or bias.
All employment-related decisions including recruitment, hiring, compensation, benefits, training, promotion, transfer, disciplinary action, and termination are based strictly on:
- Educational qualifications
- Skills and competency
- Experience
- Performance
- Professional behavior
- Leadership capability
- Business and operational requirements
The company strictly prohibits discrimination based on:
- Gender
- Age
- Religion
- Caste
- Race or ethnicity
- Nationality
- Marital status
- Disability
- Sexual orientation
- Political beliefs
- Social or economic background
- Trade union membership
- Any legally protected characteristic
The organization is committed to ensuring that every employee is treated fairly, respectfully, and professionally throughout their employment lifecycle.
Managers and supervisors are responsible for ensuring fair treatment and equal opportunity practices within their departments.
Employees who believe they have experienced discrimination or unequal treatment are encouraged to report concerns through the established grievance mechanism or HR department without fear of retaliation.

chapters.title: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Policy
chapters.text:
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. recognizes that workplace diversity contributes significantly to innovation, productivity, creativity, problem-solving, employee engagement, and long-term business sustainability.
The company values diversity in:
- Educational backgrounds
- Professional experiences
- Gender representation
- Cultural perspectives
- Skills and competencies
- Ideas and innovation
The organization is committed to building an inclusive work environment where employees feel respected, valued, and empowered to contribute fully.
To support diversity and inclusion, the company promotes:
- Inclusive recruitment and hiring practices
- Equal access to learning and development opportunities
- Fair promotion and performance evaluation systems
- Respectful workplace communication
- Women empowerment initiatives
- Awareness programs on workplace inclusion
- Equal participation opportunities across departments
Discrimination, exclusionary behavior, offensive conduct, or any practice that undermines workplace inclusivity is strictly prohibited.
## Human Rights Commitment
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. is committed to respecting and supporting internationally recognized human rights principles and ethical labor standards across all business operations.
The company believes that every employee deserves:
- Respect and dignity
- Fair treatment
- Safe working conditions
- Freedom from harassment and abuse
- Voluntary employment
- Equal opportunities
- Ethical workplace practices
The organization does not tolerate:
- Forced labor
- Bonded labor
- Child labor
- Human trafficking
- Workplace exploitation
- Physical punishment
- Mental coercion
- Intimidation or abuse
The company expects employees, contractors, suppliers, vendors, and business partners to uphold similar human rights and ethical labor standards.
Periodic audits, supplier evaluations, and compliance assessments may be conducted to ensure alignment with organizational expectations and applicable regulations.
## Child Labor and Forced Labor Policy
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. strictly prohibits all forms of child labor, forced labor, involuntary labor, bonded labor, and exploitative employment practices.
The company ensures that:
- No employee below the legally permitted working age is employed
- Employment is entirely voluntary
- Employees are free to resign in accordance with employment terms
- Employees are not subjected to coercion, intimidation, or unlawful restrictions
- Identity documents are not unlawfully retained
- Recruitment practices remain ethical and transparent
The company may verify age documentation during recruitment and onboarding processes to ensure compliance with applicable labor laws.
Any violation related to child labor or forced labor may result in immediate disciplinary action, contract termination, legal reporting, and vendor disqualification where applicable.
## Anti-Harassment and Respectful Workplace Policy
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. is committed to maintaining a workplace that promotes professionalism, dignity, inclusion, respect, and collaboration.
The company maintains a zero-tolerance approach toward:
- Harassment
- Bullying
- Workplace violence
- Intimidation
- Abusive conduct
- Threatening behavior
- Disrespectful communication
- Psychological harassment
- Offensive workplace conduct
Harassment may occur verbally, physically, visually, psychologically, electronically, or digitally.
Examples of prohibited conduct include:
- Verbal abuse or insults
- Humiliating comments
- Repeated offensive jokes
- Aggressive behavior
- Threats or intimidation
- Spreading malicious rumors
- Offensive emails or messages
- Public humiliation
- Discriminatory remarks
- Hostile work behavior
All employees are expected to:
- Treat colleagues respectfully
- Maintain professional behavior
- Promote positive teamwork
- Avoid offensive language or actions
- Support a healthy workplace environment
- Cooperate during investigations
Any employee found violating this policy may face disciplinary action including warning, suspension, termination, or legal proceedings depending on the severity of misconduct.

chapters.title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Policy
chapters.text:
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. strictly complies with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act and is committed to providing a workplace free from sexual harassment, inappropriate conduct, and gender-based misconduct.
Sexual harassment includes but is not limited to:
- Unwelcome physical contact
- Sexual advances
- Requests for sexual favors
- Sexually explicit comments
- Offensive gestures
- Inappropriate touching
- Sexually suggestive communication
- Display of explicit material
- Repeated unwanted communication
- Inappropriate digital messages or emails
The company has established an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) responsible for:
- Receiving complaints
- Conducting confidential investigations
- Protecting complainants and witnesses
- Recommending corrective actions
- Ensuring legal compliance
- Maintaining procedural fairness
All complaints are handled confidentially and investigated impartially.
Retaliation against complainants, witnesses, or participants involved in investigations is strictly prohibited.
Awareness sessions and POSH training programs may be conducted periodically for employees and management personnel.

chapters.title: Employment Categories
chapters.text:
Employees engaged with JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. may be classified under different employment categories depending on the nature, duration, and terms of employment.
[table]
| Employment Category | Description |
| Permanent Employee | Employee appointed on a regular long-term basis |
| Probationary Employee | Employee undergoing evaluation during probation period |
| Contract Employee | Employee engaged for fixed-term assignments or specific projects |
| Temporary Employee | Employee hired for temporary operational requirements |
| Trainee/Apprentice | Individual undergoing structured training |
| Intern | Student or learner engaged for internship purposes |
| Consultant | External expert engaged for specialized professional services |
Benefits, compensation structures, notice periods, and eligibility criteria may vary depending on employment classification and contractual agreements.
## Recruitment and Fair Hiring Practices
The company follows fair, transparent, and merit-based recruitment practices to attract qualified, competent, and ethical professionals.
Recruitment processes may include:
- Job requisition approval
- Job advertisement
- Resume screening
- HR interviews
- Technical interviews
- Skill assessments
- Reference verification
- Background verification
- Medical fitness evaluation where applicable
The organization strictly prohibits:
- Discriminatory hiring practices
- Unethical recruitment fees
- False employment promises
- Coercive hiring methods
Selection decisions are based on qualifications, skills, experience, cultural fit, and operational requirements.
All information provided by applicants must be accurate and authentic.
Submission of false information or forged documents may result in disqualification or termination.
## Probation and Employment Confirmation
Newly appointed employees may be placed on probation for a specified duration depending on job role, department, and business requirements.
During the probation period:
- Employee performance is evaluated
- Attendance and discipline are monitored
- Training and onboarding are conducted
- Adaptability and competency are assessed
- Compliance with company standards is reviewed
Based on evaluation outcomes, the company may:
- Confirm employment
- Extend probation
- Reassign responsibilities
- Terminate employment where necessary
Employment confirmation is communicated formally by HR or authorized management representatives.
## Employee Conduct Expectations
All employees are expected to maintain the highest standards of professional conduct, integrity, discipline, and ethical behavior while representing the organization.
Employees are expected to:
- Follow company policies and procedures
- Maintain punctuality and attendance
- Respect supervisors and colleagues
- Protect company property and information
- Follow safety and quality procedures
- Maintain workplace cleanliness and discipline
- Avoid conflicts of interest
- Support teamwork and collaboration
- Comply with GMP and regulatory requirements
- Maintain confidentiality of company information
Any conduct that negatively affects workplace discipline, safety, productivity, reputation, or employee well-being may result in disciplinary action.
## Internal Communication Policy
Effective communication plays a critical role in maintaining operational efficiency, employee engagement, teamwork, and workplace transparency.
Official communication channels may include:
- Company emails
- Notice boards
- HR circulars
- Department meetings
- Training sessions
- Digital communication systems
- Employee engagement forums
Employees are expected to:
- Read and respond to official communications
- Use professional language
- Maintain respectful interactions
- Avoid misinformation or rumor spreading
- Use company communication tools responsibly
Unauthorized disclosure of internal communication or misuse of communication platforms may result in disciplinary action.
## Dress Code, Personal Hygiene and Grooming Standards
Employees are expected to maintain appropriate personal appearance, cleanliness, and professional grooming standards suitable for their work environment and operational responsibilities.
The company recognizes that proper workplace attire and hygiene are critical not only for professionalism but also for safety, product quality, GMP compliance, and operational discipline within regulated manufacturing environments.
Employees working in office and administrative functions are expected to wear:
- Clean and professional attire
- Decent and workplace-appropriate clothing
- Identity cards during working hours
Employees working in manufacturing, warehouse, laboratory, engineering, maintenance, utilities, and quality-controlled environments may be required to wear:
- Company uniforms
- Safety shoes
- Helmets and PPE
- Hairnets, gloves, masks, and protective garments
- GMP-compliant clothing where applicable

chapters.title: Recruitment and Selection Process
chapters.text:
The Company follows a structured and merit-based recruitment process to attract and retain qualified talent.
- Job vacancies are advertised through appropriate channels to ensure equal opportunity.
- Selection is based on qualifications, experience, competencies, and organizational fit.
- Interviews and assessments are conducted using standardized and unbiased methods.
- Background verification is carried out prior to final appointment.
- The Company strictly prohibits charging any recruitment fees to candidates.
[table]
| Stage | Key Activities | Responsibility | Timeline |
| Job Posting | Vacancy advertised through portals, website, and referrals | HR Department | 2–5 days |
| Application Screening | Resume shortlisting based on eligibility | HR Team | 3–5 days |
| Interview Process | Technical & HR interviews conducted | Hiring Manager & HR | 1–2 weeks |
| Evaluation | Candidate assessment & selection | Panel | 2–3 days |
| Offer Rollout | Offer letter issued | HR | 2–3 days |
| Pre-Joining Formalities | Document verification & background check | HR | 3–7 days |
Key Principles
- No discrimination or bias in hiring
- No recruitment fees charged to candidates
- Equal opportunity for all applicants
- Strict background verification process
## Offer of Employment and Appointment
- Selected candidates are issued a formal Offer Letter outlining the key terms of employment.
- Upon acceptance, an Appointment Letter/Employment Contract is provided, detailing:
- Job title and responsibilities
- Reporting structure
- Work location
- Compensation and benefits
- Working hours and leave entitlements
- Applicable policies and code of conduct
The employment contract serves as a binding agreement between the employee and the Company.
Employees must submit all required documents during hiring. HR will issue appointment documents upon submission.
For Internship / Trainee: Interns must submit a letter from their college and comply with all company policies.
## Probation Period
- All new employees may be required to undergo a probation period, typically 180 Days, depending on the role.
- During this period:
- Performance, conduct, and suitability are evaluated
- Training and support are provided for role adaptation
- Upon successful completion, employment is confirmed in writing.
- The probation period may be extended by 90 days or employment discontinued based on performance.
[table]
| Employee Category | Notice Period |
| Helper | 30 Days |
| Chemist to Sr. Executive | 60 Days |
| Assistant Manager & Above | 90 Days |
Note: The above notice periods are applicable in cases of resignation, retirement, or completion of employment contract.

chapters.title: Working Hours and Attendance
chapters.text:
- Standard working hours are defined in accordance with operational requirements and applicable laws.
- Employees are expected to maintain punctuality and adhere to assigned schedules.
- Attendance must be recorded through designated systems.
- Absences must be communicated and approved as per company procedures.
[table]
| Parameter | Details |
| Working Days | Monday to Saturday |
| Weekly Hours | 48 hours |
| Shift Types | General / Rotational |
| Break Time | 30–60 minutes |
## Attendance System
- Biometric / digital system used
- Mandatory clock-in and clock-out
- Late coming tracked
## Attendance Rules
[table]
| Situation | Policy |
| Late Arrival | Must be recorded & justified |
| Early Leaving | Requires approval |
| Absence | Prior intimation mandatory |
| Unauthorized Absence | Subject to disciplinary action |
## Leave Entitlements
Employees are entitled to leave in accordance with company policy and legal requirements, including:
- Annual/earned leave
- Sick leave
- Casual leave
- Maternity and paternity leave
- Public holidays
All leave requests must be submitted in advance (except emergencies) and approved by the reporting manager.
[table]
| Leave Type | Eligibility | Days/Year | Carry Forward | Approval |
| Earned Leave | All employees | 12–18 | Limited | Manager |
| Sick Leave | All employees | 7–10 | No | Medical proof |
| Casual Leave | All employees | 5–7 | No | Manager |
| Maternity Leave | Female employees | As per law | NA | HR |
| Paternity Leave | Male employees | 3–5 | NA | HR |
| Public Holidays | All | As declared | NA |
## Compensation and Benefits
- Employees are compensated fairly and in compliance with statutory requirements.
- Salary structure, benefits, and deductions are clearly communicated.
- Compensation includes:
- Fixed salary components
- Allowances and statutory benefits
- Performance-based incentives
- Payments are made through bank transfer within defined timelines.
## Typical Salary Structure
[table]
| Component | Description |
| Basic Salary | Core component |
| Allowances | HRA, conveyance, etc. |
| Statutory Benefits | PF, ESI (if applicable) |
| Performance Pay | Based on role |
The organization’s working hours are determined by the day and shift. Employees must complete a minimum of 8 hours between 'Punch In' and 'Punch Out' to be considered present for a full working day. Attendance details can be viewed on the Keka mobile app. In case of discrepancies, employees must regularize their attendance within 7 days, after which the system will deduct leave.
Grace Time:
- Below Assistant Manager: 15 minutes’ grace allowed twice a month.
- Assistant Manager & Above: 30 minutes grace allowed twice a month, along with two instances of either late arrival or early departure (up to 2 hours), not on the same day. This grace is not applicable on weekly offs.

chapters.title: Transfer and Internal Mobility
chapters.text:
The Company encourages employee development through internal opportunities.
- Employees may be transferred based on:
- Business requirements
- Skill alignment
- Career development opportunities
- Transfers may involve changes in role, department, or location.
- Adequate notice and transition support are provided.

chapters.title: Wage Equality
chapters.text:
At JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd., the organization is committed to maintaining fair, transparent, and equitable compensation practices across all levels of employment. The company firmly believes in the principle of equal pay for equal work and ensures that all employees are compensated fairly based on their qualifications, experience, responsibilities, skills, competencies, and performance, irrespective of gender, religion, race, caste, disability, age, nationality, marital status, or any other legally protected characteristic.
The company continuously strives to maintain a workplace culture that promotes equality, inclusivity, fairness, and professional respect. Compensation practices are designed to ensure that employees performing similar roles with comparable responsibilities receive equitable remuneration in accordance with company standards and market practices.
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. conducts periodic compensation reviews to identify and eliminate any unintended pay disparities and to ensure alignment with applicable labor laws, industry benchmarks, and organizational objectives.
The company’s wage equality framework includes the following initiatives:
- Annual review of compensation structures and pay practices to identify any disparities or inconsistencies.
- Merit-based salary increments and promotion systems linked to performance evaluations and competency development.
- Transparent compensation structures designed to maintain fairness across departments and employee categories.
- Equal access to training, development, promotion, and leadership opportunities for all eligible employees.
- Confidential grievance mechanisms through which employees may raise concerns related to compensation or discrimination without fear of retaliation.
- Periodic internal audits to ensure compliance with legal and ethical employment standards.
Employees are encouraged to report concerns regarding wage equality, discrimination, or unfair employment practices through HR or the Grievance Redressal Committee. All such concerns are handled confidentially, professionally, and without prejudice.
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. maintains a structured and transparent compensation framework designed to ensure statutory compliance, employee welfare, competitive remuneration, and long-term financial security for employees.
The salary structure is designed considering:
- Nature of the role and responsibilities
- Technical competency and experience
- Industry standards and market competitiveness
- Statutory compliance requirements
- Organizational performance and business sustainability
The salary package may include fixed compensation, statutory benefits, performance-based incentives, allowances, and other applicable benefits depending on the employee category and role.
The major components of the salary structure are explained below:
## Basic Salary
The Basic Salary forms the fixed and core component of the employee’s compensation structure and serves as the basis for calculating various statutory contributions and employee benefits.
- Basic salary generally constitutes approximately 40% to 50% of the total Cost to Company (CTC), depending upon the employee grade and designation.
- It is used for calculation of Provident Fund (PF), Gratuity, Bonus, and other statutory benefits wherever applicable.
- The basic salary amount is determined based on job role, qualifications, experience, internal parity, and compensation policies.
The company periodically reviews salary structures to maintain competitiveness and compliance with labor regulations.
## House Rent Allowance (HRA)
House Rent Allowance is provided to employees to support accommodation and housing-related expenses.
- HRA is generally calculated as a percentage of the basic salary.
- Employees residing in metro cities may receive a higher HRA component as compared to employees in non-metro locations.
- HRA exemptions and tax applicability shall be governed by prevailing income tax regulations and employee declarations.
The company may revise HRA structures depending on employee category, work location, and applicable statutory changes.
## Special Allowance
Special Allowance is a flexible component included within the salary structure to balance the overall compensation package.
- It may vary depending upon employee role, designation, experience, and salary structure planning.
- This allowance may also be used to optimize compensation structures in line with applicable tax regulations.
- Special allowances may cover additional compensation components not specifically categorized under other allowances.
The amount and structure of special allowance shall remain subject to management discretion and compensation policy revisions.
## Bonus and Performance-Linked Incentives

chapters.title: Gratuity
chapters.text:
Employees who complete continuous service as prescribed under applicable laws shall be eligible for gratuity benefits.
Gratuity is paid as a long-term statutory benefit to employees upon resignation, retirement, superannuation, permanent disability, or death, subject to eligibility conditions.
## Explanation of the Formula
- Last Drawn Salary generally includes Basic Salary and Dearness Allowance where applicable.
- Fifteen days’ salary is considered for every completed year of service.
- The divisor 26 represents the average working days in a month.
Additional provisions:
- Employees generally become eligible for gratuity after completing five years of continuous service, subject to applicable laws.
- Gratuity payments shall comply with the Payment of Gratuity Act and applicable tax regulations.
- Tax exemptions may apply as per prevailing income tax provisions.
## Overtime and Compensatory Off
Employees may occasionally be required to work beyond normal working hours in order to support manufacturing schedules, maintenance shutdowns, audits, customer commitments, emergencies, or operational requirements.
Eligible employees working beyond scheduled working hours may receive overtime compensation in accordance with applicable labor laws and company policy.

chapters.title: Overtime Compensation
chapters.text:
- Overtime work must generally receive prior approval from the reporting supervisor or authorized department head.
- Overtime compensation rates shall be calculated as per statutory provisions and applicable company policy.
- Employees working on weekly offs, public holidays, or during emergency operational requirements may become eligible for overtime pay or compensatory off.
Employees who work on approved holidays or weekly offs may be eligible for compensatory leave subject to operational approval.
[table]
| Aspect | Details |
| Eligibility | Employees working on approved holidays or overtime schedules |
| Approval Requirement | Prior supervisor approval mandatory |
| Utilization Period | Comp-off should generally be utilized within specified timelines |
| Encashment | Subject to company policy and approval |
| Operational Consideration | Approval subject to departmental workload and business continuity |
Unused compensatory offs may lapse if not utilized within the prescribed validity period.
## Other Allowances and Benefits
Depending upon employee role, department, location, and operational requirements, the company may provide additional allowances or support benefits.
These may include:
- Telephone or internet reimbursement for official work purposes
- Meal or canteen facilities
- Uniforms and safety equipment
- Shift allowance
- Travel reimbursement
- Training and development support
- Special role-based allowances
- Relocation assistance where applicable
Such benefits may vary depending on employee designation, operational needs, and company policies.
## EPF and ESI Contributions
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. complies with all statutory obligations related to Employee Provident Fund (EPF) and Employee State Insurance (ESI) in order to support employee financial security, healthcare access, and social welfare benefits.
## Employee Provident Fund (EPF)
EPF contributions are made in accordance with applicable statutory regulations.
- Both employee and employer contribute prescribed percentages toward the EPF account.
- Contributions accumulate in the employee’s EPF account and may be withdrawn subject to EPFO regulations.
- EPF provides long-term financial security and retirement savings support.
## Benefits of EPF
- Retirement savings accumulation
- Pension-related benefits
- Partial withdrawal provisions under specified conditions
- Financial support during emergencies
## Employee State Insurance (ESI)
Eligible employees are covered under the ESI scheme as prescribed by statutory guidelines.
ESI benefits may include:
- Medical treatment and hospitalization
- Disability benefits
- Maternity benefits
- Dependent benefits
- Sickness compensation
- Work injury compensation
[table]
| Scheme | Eligibility | Contribution | Benefits |
| EPF | As per statutory applicability | Employee and employer contributions as prescribed | Retirement and financial security benefits |
| ESI | Employees within prescribed wage limits | Statutory contribution rates | Medical and insurance benefits |
Employees may access EPF and ESI information through official government portals or HR support channels.

## Payment Schedule
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. ensures timely processing and payment of employee salaries and statutory contributions.
- Salaries are generally credited before or on 7th day of each month.
- Salary payments are made through bank transfer directly into employee salary accounts.
- Employees receive salary slips through digital or authorized HR systems.
- Approved overtime payments, incentives, reimbursements, and bonuses are processed separately based on eligibility and approval timelines.

chapters.title: Leave Policy
chapters.text:
- Privilege Leave (PL): 15 days annually; accrued at 1.25 days per 20 working days.
- Casual Leave (CL): 6 days annually; accrued at 0.5 days per 20 working days.
- Medical Leave: In case of serious injury at work, medical leave may be granted based on the doctor’s recommendation.
- PL can be carried forward up to 15 PL the next calendar year.
## Official Holiday Policy
06 festival holidays will be declared annually by HR. National Holidays: 26th January and 15th August. Religious Holidays: Dhuleti, Janmashtami, Diwali, New Year. Employees working on an official holiday, with prior HOD approval, will receive:
- 1+2 days’ compensation (Below Assistant Manager)
- 1-day Comp-Off (Assistant Manager & Above)

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangements
chapters.text:
The Company recognizes that flexible work arrangements can improve employee productivity, work-life balance, employee engagement, and retention while ensuring business continuity and operational effectiveness. Flexible work arrangements may be approved where they are compatible with business requirements and job responsibilities.
Applies to all permanent employees whose roles can be effectively performed under a flexible work arrangement without adversely impacting safety, productivity, quality, customer service, or team collaboration.
[table]
| Type | Description |
| Flexible Working Hours (Flexi-time) | Employees may vary their start and end times while completing the required daily |
| Hybrid Working | Employees work partly from the office and partly from an approved remote locatio |
| Remote Working | Employees perform their duties from an approved remote location on a regular or  |
| Compressed Work Week | Employees complete their standard weekly working hours in fewer working days (e. |
| Part-Time Work | Employees work fewer hours than the standard full-time schedule based on busines |
| Job Sharing | Two employees share the responsibilities of one full-time position. |
## Eligibility Criteria
Employees may be eligible for flexible work arrangements if:
- They have successfully completed their probation period.
- Their job responsibilities can be effectively performed under the requested arrangement.
- Their performance rating meets company expectations.
- The arrangement does not negatively impact operational requirements, customer commitments, safety, quality, or team effectiveness.
- Adequate communication and technological resources are available.
## Request and Approval Process
- Employee submits a formal request to the reporting manager.
- Immediate supervisor reviews operational feasibility.
- Department Head and HR review the request.
- Final approval is granted by the authorized management representative.
- Approved arrangements shall be documented and communicated to all relevant stakeholders.
## Employee Responsibilities
Employees approved for flexible work arrangements shall:
- Maintain agreed working hours and availability.
- Meet performance, productivity, and quality expectations.
- Attend meetings, training programs, and business activities as required.
- Ensure confidentiality and protection of company information.
- Comply with all company policies, including health, safety, and cybersecurity requirements.
## Manager Responsibilities
Managers shall:
- Evaluate requests objectively and consistently.
- Ensure business continuity and adequate team coverage.
- Monitor employee performance and productivity.
- Conduct periodic reviews of approved arrangements.
- Modify or discontinue arrangements if business needs require.
## Resources and Support
The Company may provide:
- Secure access to company systems and networks.
- Communication and collaboration tools.
- IT support for remote working requirements.
- Training on effective remote and flexible working practices.
## Review and Termination
- Flexible work arrangements shall be reviewed periodically, at least annually or as required.
- The Company reserves the right to modify, suspend, or terminate any arrangement due to operational, performance, safety, or business requirements.
- Employees may request changes to approved arrangements through the established approval process.
## Records
HR shall maintain records of all approved flexible work arrangements, review outcomes, and related documentation.

chapters.title: Learning and Development Programs
chapters.text:
We believe that our employees' growth is inseparable from our organizational success. We are committed to investing in skills, performance, and career development for every team member.
## Workforce Skill Enhancement Training
A comprehensive training framework ensures every employee has access to the learning opportunities they need to excel.
[table]
| Training Module | Target Audience | Frequency |
| New Employee Orientation & Onboarding | All new joiners | Day 1 and first week |
| GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices) | Production & QC staff | Annual + refresher |
| Occupational Health & Safety | All employees | Annual mandatory |
| Skill Development - Technical | Role-specific | Ongoing / as required |
| Soft Skills (Communication, Teamwork, Leadership) | All employees | Bi-annual |
| Information & Data Security Awareness | All employees | Annual |
| Anti-Corruption & Ethics | All employees | Annual |
| Child Labor, Forced Labor & Human Rights Awareness | All employees + contractors | Annual |
| Diversity, Inclusion & Anti-Harassment | All employees | Annual |
| Emergency & Crisis Management | All employees | Annual drill |
| Environmental & Sustainability Practices | All employees | Annual |
| Leadership Development | Supervisors & above | Ongoing |
- Training records including attendance, certifications, and completion status are maintained in each employee's personal file.
- External certifications and professional development courses aligned with job roles may be sponsored by the company subject to approval.
- Online learning platforms are made available to employees for self-paced learning on a range of technical and soft skill topics.
## Periodic Performance Review Process
A structured and transparent performance management system ensures that every employee's contributions are recognized and areas for improvement are identified and supported.
- Objective Setting: At the start of each performance cycle, employees and their managers jointly set measurable KPIs and performance goals aligned with departmental and organizational objectives.
- Mid-Year Review: A structured mid-year check-in to assess progress, provide feedback, adjust objectives if required, and address any performance concerns early.
- End-of-Year Appraisal: A comprehensive annual evaluation against agreed KPIs and competencies. The appraisal is documented, signed by both parties, and filed with HR.
- Self-Assessment: Employees are invited to submit a self-assessment reflecting on their achievements, challenges, and development goals, forming the basis for a constructive discussion with their manager.
- Rating Scale: Performance is rated on a defined scale (e.g., Exceptional / Meets Expectations / Needs Improvement) with clear descriptors for each level.
- 360-Degree Feedback: For supervisory and senior roles, feedback from peers, direct reports, and cross-functional colleagues supplements the manager's assessment.
## ndividual Development & Career Plan
Every employee is entitled to a personalized career development plan that reflects their aspirations and the company's talent needs.
- Career development discussions are held during the annual appraisal and, where needed, separately.
- Each employee works with their manager to create a plan outlining short-term skill goals, long-term career aspirations, training requirements, and potential advancement pathways.
- The company provides mentorship pairing, where employees are matched with experienced colleagues or senior leaders to support their professional journey.
- High-potential employees are identified and enrolled in accelerated development programs to prepare them for future leadership roles.
- Succession planning is actively practiced to ensure continuity in critical roles and to provide internal growth opportunities.
## Career Movement Initiatives
We value and actively promote movement within the organization as a means of professional enrichment and talent retention.
- Internal Job Postings: All vacancies are shared internally before external hiring, giving existing employees the first opportunity to apply.
- Vertical Mobility: Employees demonstrating consistent performance and readiness are considered for promotion to higher-level roles through the appraisal and succession planning process.
- Horizontal Mobility: Cross-departmental transfers are supported to help employees broaden their expertise and contribute to different parts of the business.
- Transversal Mobility: Cross-training and skill development programs allow employees to acquire skills applicable across multiple functions, enhancing versatility.
- Transfer Requests: Employees wishing to transfer to a different department or facility may submit a formal request to HR. Requests are reviewed based on business needs, employee skills, and development goals.
- Company-initiated transfers are communicated at least two weeks in advance with full details of the new role and any applicable changes.

chapters.title: Technology And Information Security
chapters.text:
## Purpose and Organizational Commitment
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. recognizes that technology systems, digital infrastructure, operational data, manufacturing records, research information, and confidential business documents are critical assets of the organization. The company is committed to maintaining secure, reliable, and efficient technology systems while protecting organizational information from unauthorized access, misuse, disclosure, alteration, theft, cyber threats, operational disruption, or loss.
As part of its commitment toward operational excellence, regulatory compliance, customer confidence, and business continuity, the organization has established technology and information security policies applicable to all employees, contractors, consultants, trainees, temporary staff, and third-party personnel who access company systems, networks, devices, records, or digital resources.
The purpose of this policy is to:
- Protect confidential business and operational information
- Maintain integrity and security of digital systems
- Prevent unauthorized access to company data
- Support safe and responsible use of technology resources
- Ensure compliance with legal, contractual, and regulatory obligations
- Minimize cybersecurity and operational risks
- Protect intellectual property and technical information
- Support secure communication and data handling practices
All employees are expected to understand and comply with technology and information security requirements while using company systems and resources.
## Acceptable Use of Technology Resources
Technology resources provided by JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. are intended primarily for official business and operational purposes. Employees are expected to use all company-provided systems responsibly, ethically, securely, and in accordance with company policies.
Technology resources may include:
- Desktop computers and laptops
- Servers and network systems
- Company email accounts
- Internet and Wi-Fi access
- ERP and operational software systems
- Production monitoring systems
- Laboratory and technical systems
- Printers and scanners
- Mobile phones and communication devices
- Cloud-based applications and storage systems
- CCTV and access control systems
Employees are expected to:
- Use company systems only for authorized work-related purposes
- Protect company devices from misuse or damage
- Follow IT and cybersecurity procedures
- Avoid activities that may compromise network security or operational continuity
- Maintain professionalism while using communication systems
- Use licensed and approved software only
- Safeguard confidential and sensitive information
Limited personal use of company systems may be permitted where such use:
- Does not interfere with work responsibilities
- Does not compromise security or productivity
- Does not violate company policies or legal requirements
- Does not create excessive network or operational burden
The company reserves the right to restrict or prohibit any activity that may negatively impact operational efficiency, information security, or organizational reputation.
## User Access Control and Password Security
Access to company systems, applications, operational software, and confidential information shall be granted only to authorized personnel based on job responsibilities and operational requirements.
Employees are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality and security of their login credentials and access privileges.
Employees shall:
- Use strong and secure passwords
- Keep passwords confidential
- Change passwords periodically where required
- Log out from systems when not in use
- Prevent unauthorized access to company devices
- Report suspected unauthorized access immediately
Employees shall not:
- Share passwords with unauthorized persons
- Use another employee’s login credentials
- Attempt to bypass system security controls
- Access systems or information without authorization
- Store passwords openly or insecurely
The company may implement additional security measures such as:
- Multi-factor authentication
- Access restrictions
- Role-based permissions
- System activity monitoring
- Password expiry requirements
Any unauthorized access attempt or misuse of access privileges may result in disciplinary and legal action.
## Confidential Information and Data Protection
Employees may have access to confidential, proprietary, technical, operational, financial, customer-related, or commercially sensitive information during the course of their employment.
Confidential information may include:
- Product formulations and specifications
- Manufacturing processes
- Research and development data
- Quality control records
- Customer and supplier information
- Pricing and commercial agreements
- Financial reports and business strategies
- Regulatory and audit documentation
- Employee records and payroll information
- Technical documentation and operational procedures

chapters.title: Exit Policies
chapters.text:
## Types of Employment Separation
Employment separation from JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. may occur under various circumstances including voluntary resignation, retirement, termination, contract completion, abandonment of employment, or separation due to business or operational requirements.
The major categories of separation include:
[table]
| Type of Separation | Description |
| Voluntary Resignation | Employee voluntarily resigns from employment |
| Retirement | Separation upon reaching retirement age or voluntary retirement |
| Termination | Separation initiated by the company due to misconduct, performance, or operation |
| Completion of Contract | End of fixed-term or contractual employment |
| Probation Non-Confirmation | Separation during or after probation evaluation |
| Absconding / Job Abandonment | Unauthorized absence without communication |
| Medical Separation | Separation due to medical inability to continue employment |
| Redundancy / Business Restructuring | Separation due to operational or organizational restructuring |
The company reserves the right to determine the appropriate category of separation based on employment circumstances and applicable organizational policies.
## Employee Resignation Process
Employees wishing to resign from the organization are required to submit a formal written resignation letter or email to their reporting manager and Human Resources Department.
The resignation communication should include:
- Employee name and designation
- Employee ID
- Department
- Proposed last working date
- Reason for resignation (optional but encouraged)
- Handover status or transition plan where applicable
Employees are expected to maintain professionalism and cooperation throughout the resignation and transition process.
The company encourages employees to discuss concerns or career decisions with their supervisors or HR before finalizing resignation decisions wherever appropriate.
## Notice Period Requirements
Employees separating voluntarily from employment are generally required to serve a notice period as specified in their appointment letter, employment contract, or applicable company policy.
The standard notice period may vary depending upon:
- Employee grade or designation
- Departmental role
- Operational responsibilities
- Employment category
- Contractual agreements
Employees are expected to:
- Continue performing duties responsibly during the notice period
- Support transition and knowledge transfer activities
- Complete pending assignments and documentation
- Cooperate in operational handover processes
The company may, at its discretion:
- Require full notice period service
- Approve partial notice period completion
- Recover notice pay in lieu of unserved notice period
- Waive notice requirements under special circumstances
Similarly, the company may provide notice or salary in lieu of notice during company-initiated separation where applicable under law or employment agreements.
## Handover and Knowledge Transfer Responsibilities
Employees separating from the organization are responsible for ensuring proper handover of duties, records, operational responsibilities, and company assets before their last working day.
The handover process may include:
- Transfer of ongoing assignments and responsibilities
- Submission of project status updates
- Transfer of operational records and documentation
- Sharing of passwords or access information through authorized procedures
- Handover of customer, vendor, or operational communications
- Completion of pending approvals or reports
- Return of company property and equipment
Supervisors and department heads may review and verify completion of handover activities before clearance approval.
Employees are expected to cooperate fully during transition processes in order to minimize operational disruption and ensure business continuity.
## Return of Company Property and Assets
Before separation from employment, employees are required to return all company-owned property, materials, systems, records, and equipment issued during the course of employment.
Company property may include:
- Identity cards and access cards
- Laptops, desktops, or mobile devices
- Company documents and files
- Uniforms and PPE
- Tools, instruments, or equipment
- Keys and security devices
- Storage devices or confidential records
- Company vehicles where applicable
Employees are expected to return company property in good condition subject to reasonable wear and tear.
The company reserves the right to recover costs associated with:
- Lost or damaged property
- Unreturned assets
- Unauthorized retention of company materials
- Financial liabilities arising from negligence or misuse
Final settlement may be withheld partially or fully until all company assets and obligations are cleared.

chapters.title: Whistleblower Procedure
chapters.text:
## Reporting of Unethical Practices and Misconduct
JRS Pharma & Gujarat Microwax Pvt. Ltd. is committed to conducting its business activities with the highest standards of integrity, transparency, accountability, and ethical behavior. The organization encourages employees and stakeholders to report any actual or suspected unethical conduct, misconduct, illegal activities, fraud, corruption, policy violations, or improper business practices that may adversely affect the company, its employees, customers, stakeholders, operations, or reputation.
The Whistleblower Procedure is established to provide employees with a secure, confidential, and reliable mechanism for reporting concerns relating to unethical or improper activities observed within the organization.
Employees are encouraged to report concerns in good faith whenever they become aware of activities that may involve:
- Fraudulent practices or financial irregularities
- Corruption or bribery
- Theft, embezzlement, or misuse of company property
- Falsification of records or documents
- Violation of company policies or legal requirements
- Workplace harassment or abuse of authority
- Conflict of interest
- Unsafe operational practices
- Environmental violations
- Data security or confidentiality breaches
- Regulatory non-compliance
- Ethical misconduct or inappropriate business practices
- Intentional concealment of wrongdoing
The company encourages early reporting of concerns so that appropriate corrective and preventive actions can be taken promptly.
## Reporting Channels
Employees may report concerns through any of the following authorized channels:
[table]
| Reporting Channel | Contact Point |
| Immediate Supervisor | Department Reporting Manager |
| Human Resources Department | HR Representative / HR Manager |
| Department Head | Functional Head |
| Senior Management | Authorized Management Personnel |
| Email | ID |
Employees are encouraged to provide factual, clear, and complete information while reporting concerns, including:
- Nature of the concern
- Date and location of incident
- Individuals involved
- Supporting documents or evidence if available
- Any witnesses or relevant information
Reports may be submitted verbally or in writing depending upon the seriousness and sensitivity of the matter.
